title: The army returns
summary: The king’s army returns after searching in vain for the people of the Lord. Its forces are reduced, and division begins among the remaining people.

explicit_facts.text: The king’s army returned after searching in vain for the people of the Lord.
The king’s forces were small after being reduced, and division began among the remainder of the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The returning army and divided people can be shown together in a settlement or gathering place.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise location, architecture, clothing, and appearance of the people are not stated.

narration.text: the army of the king returned
there began to be a division among the remainder of the people

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the searched-for people as present; the search was in vain.

title: Gideon draws his sword
summary: The lesser part begins threatening the king, and great contention begins among them. Gideon draws his sword and swears in wrath that he will slay the king.

explicit_facts.text: The lesser part began threatening the king, and great contention began among them.
Gideon was a strong man and an enemy of the king. He drew his sword and swore in wrath that he would slay the king.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gideon can be shown drawing his sword among people in contention.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, appearances, and the king’s physical presence are not stated.

narration.text: And the lesser part began to breathe out threatenings against the king, and there began to be a great contention among them.
And now there was a man among them whose name was Gideon, and he being a strong man and an enemy to the king, therefore he drew his sword, and swore in his wrath that he would slay the king.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words of Gideon’s oath.
Do not assume the king is physically present.

title: The king flees to the tower
summary: Gideon fights the king. As the king is about to be overpowered, he flees to a tower near the temple. Gideon pursues, and the king sees the Lamanite army within Shemlon’s borders.

explicit_facts.text: Gideon fought with the king; when the king saw he was about to be overpowered, he fled and got upon a tower near the temple.
Gideon pursued the king and was about to get upon the tower to slay him; the king looked toward Shemlon and saw the Lamanite army within the borders of the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The tower can be shown near a temple, with the Lamanite army visible in the distant direction of Shemlon.
unspecified_visual_details: The tower and temple’s design and the army’s distance are not stated.

narration.text: he fled and ran and got upon the tower which was near the temple
the army of the Lamanites were within the borders of the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lamanites already fighting in this moment.

title: The king begs for his life
summary: The king cries out to Gideon to spare him because the Lamanites are upon them. Gideon spares the king’s life.

explicit_facts.text: The king cried out in anguish and asked Gideon to spare him, saying the Lamanites were upon them and would destroy them and his people.
The king was more concerned about his own life than his people; Gideon spared his life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gideon can be shown holding back from striking the king.
unspecified_visual_details: The characters’ expressions and exact postures are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Gideon, spare me, for the Lamanites are upon us, and they will destroy us; yea, they will destroy my people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Noah

narration.text: Gideon did spare his life

prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the king’s concern as selfless; the text says he was more concerned about his own life.

title: Flight into the wilderness
summary: The king orders the people to flee and leads them into the wilderness with their women and children. The Lamanites pursue, overtake them, and begin to slay them.

explicit_facts.text: The king commanded the people to flee before the Lamanites, went before them, and they fled into the wilderness with their women and children.
The Lamanites pursued and overtook them, and began to slay them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The pursuit and attack may be shown without graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The number of people and the wilderness terrain are not stated.

narration.text: they did flee into the wilderness, with their women and their children
began to slay them

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Men are ordered to flee
summary: The king orders all men to leave their wives and children and flee. Many refuse and choose to stay with their families; the rest leave and flee.

explicit_facts.text: The king commanded all the men to leave their wives and children and flee before the Lamanites.
Many would not leave their families and chose to stay and perish with them; the rest left their wives and children and fled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The men’s separation into those who stay and those who flee can be shown at the moment of decision.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and number of the men in either group are not stated.

narration.text: all the men should leave their wives and their children
many that would not leave them

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue or individual biographies for the men.

title: The daughters plead
summary: Those who stayed cause their fair daughters to stand forth and plead with the Lamanites not to slay them. The Lamanites have compassion, charmed by the women’s beauty.

explicit_facts.text: Those who stayed with their wives and children caused their fair daughters to stand forth and plead with the Lamanites not to slay them.
The Lamanites had compassion because they were charmed with the beauty of the women.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The daughters can be shown standing before the Lamanites in a plea.
unspecified_visual_details: The women’s appearance beyond the stated beauty, and the Lamanites’ identities, are not specified.

narration.text: stand forth and plead with the Lamanites
the Lamanites had compassion on them

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the daughters’ spoken words.

title: Captives and tribute conditions
summary: The Lamanites spare the people, take them captive, and carry them to the land of Nephi. They grant them possession of the land under conditions: surrender King Noah, deliver half their property and valuables, and pay yearly tribute. Limhi is among the captives.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites spared the people, took them captive, and carried them back to the land of Nephi.

The people could possess the land if they delivered King Noah to the Lamanites, gave half their property including half their gold and silver and all their precious things, and paid yearly tribute to the Lamanite king.
Limhi, one of the king’s sons, was among those taken captive.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The captives may be shown arriving in the land of Nephi under Lamanite custody.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, precise location, and Limhi’s appearance are not stated.

narration.text: took them captives and carried them back to the land of Nephi
one of the sons of the king among those that were taken captive

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The conditions are reported; do not present them as newly spoken dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict King Noah as present among the captives.

title: Limhi’s concern for his father
summary: Limhi desires that his father not be destroyed, though he knows his father’s iniquities; Limhi himself is just.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi desired that his father not be destroyed, was not ignorant of his father’s iniquities, and was himself just.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Limhi may be shown alone or among the captives in a reflective moment.
unspecified_visual_details: Limhi’s expression, posture, and precise location are not stated.

narration.text: Limhi was desirous that his father should not be destroyed
he himself being a just man

prohibited_inventions: Do not show King Noah physically present in this reflective moment.

title: Gideon’s search party
summary: Gideon secretly sends men into the wilderness to find the king and his people. They meet the people there, all except the king and his priests. The people had sworn to return and seek revenge if their families and those who stayed were slain.

explicit_facts.text: Gideon secretly sent men into the wilderness to search for the king and those with him; they met the people there, all except the king and his priests.
The people had sworn in their hearts to return to the land of Nephi and seek revenge if their wives, children, and those who stayed with them were slain, and also perish with them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gideon’s men can be shown meeting the people in the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: The text does not specify who among the people is visible during the meeting.

narration.text: they met the people in the wilderness
they had sworn in their hearts that they would return to the land of Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The oath is reported as being in their hearts, not spoken aloud.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the king or priests at the meeting.

title: The king dies; the priests flee
summary: The king commands them not to return. Angry with him, they cause his death by fire. They are about to put the priests to death, but the priests flee.

explicit_facts.text: The king commanded them not to return.
They were angry with the king and caused him to suffer unto death by fire.
They were about to put the priests to death, and the priests fled before them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king's death by fire can be shown without gore.
The priests can be shown fleeing from those who were about to put them to death.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the manner of the death by fire, and the priests' route are not specified.

narration.text: they were angry with the king
they fled before them.

prohibited_inventions: Do not give the king or the unnamed group names not supplied in these verses.
Do not portray the priests as killed.
Do not add wounds, blood, or other details of the death by fire.

title: The search party reports the terms
summary: As the people are about to return to the land of Nephi, they meet Gideon’s men, who tell them their families were spared and the Lamanites allowed them to possess the land by paying half their possessions. The people report that they killed the king and the priests fled farther into the wilderness.

explicit_facts.text: As the people were about to return to the land of Nephi, they met Gideon’s men, who told them what had happened to their wives and children and that the Lamanites granted possession of the land for half their possessions as tribute.
The people told Gideon’s men they had slain the king and his priests had fled farther into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two groups can be shown meeting and conveying the reported news.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s precise words and the manner of their exchange are not stated.

narration.text: they met the men of Gideon
they had slain the king, and his priests had fled from them farther into the wilderness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The deaths and family news are reported here, not reenacted.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the killing of the king or the sparing of families as occurring in this scene.

title: The people return rejoicing
summary: After they had ended the ceremony, the people return to the land of Nephi, rejoicing that their wives and children were not slain, and tell Gideon what they did to the king.

explicit_facts.text: After they had ended the ceremony, the people returned to the land of Nephi, rejoicing that their wives and children were not slain, and told Gideon what they had done to the king.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The return may be shown with the people rejoicing.
unspecified_visual_details: The ceremony’s nature and the people’s appearance are not stated.

narration.text: they returned to the land of Nephi, rejoicing
their wives and their children were not slain

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The ceremony is mentioned but not described; do not invent its actions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent ceremony details or dialogue to Gideon.

title: Oaths and Limhi’s kingdom
summary: The Lamanite king swears that his people will not slay the people. Limhi, given the kingdom by the people, swears to pay the Lamanite king half of all they possess.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanite king swore that his people should not slay the people.
The people conferred the kingdom upon Limhi, who swore to the Lamanite king that his people would pay half of all they possessed as tribute.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two oaths may be shown as separate actions within this sequence, without invented wording.
unspecified_visual_details: The ceremony or gestures accompanying the oaths are not stated.

narration.text: the king of the Lamanites made an oath unto them
having the kingdom conferred upon him by the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The oath terms are reported; no dialogue is supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent wording or ritual for either oath.

title: Peace under watch
summary: Limhi establishes the kingdom and peace among his people. The Lamanite king places guards around the land to prevent their departure and supports the guards with tribute. Limhi’s kingdom has continual peace for two years, without Lamanite molestation or attempts to destroy them.

explicit_facts.text: Limhi began to establish the kingdom and peace among his people.
The Lamanite king set guards around the land to keep Limhi’s people from departing into the wilderness and supported the guards with tribute received from the Nephites.
Limhi had continual peace in his kingdom for two years; the Lamanites did not molest them or seek to destroy them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Guards may be shown stationed around the land while the people live under Limhi’s rule.
unspecified_visual_details: The guards’ number, placement, and appearance, and the passage of the two years, are not specified.

narration.text: Limhi began to establish the kingdom
set guards round about the land
continual peace in his kingdom for the space of two years

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the guards as attacking the people or the Lamanites as molesting them during this period.
